description: Imports Ada AI-chatbot support data — conversations, messages, knowledge articles/sources/tags, and platform integrations — from a customer's Ada bot instance.

placeholders.bot_handle: user-supplied `bot_handle` endpoint config field (the subdomain of the customer's Ada bot dashboard)

spec.apiVersionPinning: path segment `/api/v2` baked into the base URL builder

configFields.name: bot_handle
configFields.description: The Ada bot handle, taken from the bot dashboard URL {BOT_HANDLE}.ada.support; also forms the API host.

configFields.name: start_date
configFields.description: UTC RFC3339 datetime; data before it is not replicated. Defaults to 12 months ago, which is also Ada's export retention limit.

configFields.name: credentials.access_token
configFields.description: Ada API key, sent as an Authorization: Bearer token.

configFields.name: interval
configFields.description: CDK-generic ISO-8601 duration between updates for this binding; connector defaults are PT15M (full refresh) and PT5M (incremental).

authTierRationale: The only credential mode is a single self-serve Ada API key (a 'Private App Credentials' access token) plus the bot handle. `oauth2=None` is returned in the connector spec and `TokenSource(oauth_spec=None, credentials=config.credentials)` is constructed with the CDK's plain `AccessToken` model, which the CDK forwards verbatim as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` with no token exchange or refresh. No OAuth app registration and no refresh token are required, and no hosted control plane is involved.

unionMisfits.description: The export endpoints are queried in bounded time WINDOWS, not as an open-ended 'everything since X'. Each request carries both a lower and an upper time bound, the window is capped at 59 days (Ada's real limit is 60), the incremental leg additionally holds the upper bound back by a 48-hour eventual-consistency lag, and the backfill start is clamped forward to now-365d because of Ada's export retention limit. PullSpec has `incrementalParam` for the lower bound only, so the upper bound, the window cap, the lag, and the retention clamp have nowhere to live except free-text `params`.

The export paginator's cursor parameter name is not a connector constant — it is per-stream (`updated_since` for conversations, `created_since` for messages) and it is the SAME parameter that carries the incremental lower bound. Pagination therefore works by advancing the query's own lower time bound rather than by a distinct page token, so `paginator.cursorParam` and `incrementalParam.param` deliberately collide. The token value is also a timestamp with meaning, not an opaque page token.

Records are not parsed from a materialised JSON body; the connector streams the response through an incremental JSON processor keyed on the JSON path `data.item` (array-element notation), then reads the leftover envelope (`meta.next_page_uri`) after the array is exhausted. `recordsPath: "data"` is the closest fit but loses the fact that pagination state is only available AFTER the record stream is drained.

The endpoint config declares `credentials` with a pydantic discriminator (`credentials_title`) over a one-member union (only `ApiKey`). This is the CDK's multi-mode credential shape used with a single mode, which is a forward-compatibility hook rather than a real alternative — the emitted spec still renders a `oneOf` with one branch.

The per-binding interval is a default written into the discovered binding's `ResourceConfig` (PT15M / PT5M) and is user-editable after discovery; it is not a schedule the connector enforces. There is no connector-wide default at all.

The four full-refresh streams are opened with the CDK's `fetch_snapshot` + an explicit tombstone document (`_meta.op = "d"`), so each sweep re-emits the whole collection and tombstones anything that disappeared. Their key is the synthetic `/_meta/row_id`, meaning row identity is positional within a sweep and not stable across sweeps.

abstained.streams[].pull.*.paginator.pageSize: No page-size or limit parameter is ever set by the connector for either the snapshot or the export endpoints; page size is entirely server-decided and never appears in the source.
abstained.streams[].pull.*.paginator.pageSizeParam: Same — the connector never sends a limit/per_page parameter, and the API's parameter name for one (if any) is not referenced anywhere in the connector.
abstained.transports[0].spec.defaultHeaders: No connector-level default headers are set; the only header added is the CDK's Authorization header derived from TokenSource.
abstained.streams[0..3].cursorField: The four full-refresh streams re-read the whole collection each sweep with no time or id filter; no cursor field exists.
abstained.streams[0..3].primaryKey (natural key): Records are keyed on the synthetic /_meta/row_id; the connector never names a natural id field for articles, sources, tags, or platform_integrations, and the document model is `extra=allow` with no declared fields.
abstained.execution.defaultSchedule: There is no connector-wide schedule. Intervals exist only as per-binding ResourceConfig defaults (PT15M / PT5M) that the user can change after discovery.
abstained.streams[].pull.*.paginator.terminateOn (: The loop terminates when `meta` or `meta.next_page_uri` is absent, and the snapshot loop additionally returns on an empty-string cursor. Whether the API also signals exhaustion via a short page or a total count is not observable from the connector source.
abstained.rateLimits: No rate-limit handling, retry policy, or concurrency cap is expressed in the connector; any such behaviour lives in the shared CDK HTTP layer and is not connector-specific.
abstained.streams[].pull.backfill vs incremental d: Backfill and incremental hit the identical path with the identical parameter names; they differ only in which bound the CDK supplies (page cursor vs log cursor) and in the retention clamp applied on the backfill leg.
